## Problem

The POST /api/events endpoint (bd-2bt) should not be open to arbitrary callers. Need basic auth to prevent accidental or malicious event injection.

## Implementation options

1. **Shared secret** — NEEDLE includes a bearer token, FABRIC validates it
   - NEEDLE: `FABRIC_AUTH_TOKEN` env var, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

issue.description:
Confirmed live 2026-07-30: fabric-watchdog.service (the systemd --user timer/service pair added specifically to auto-detect and restart a broken fabric-web, per closed bead bf-38msk) has been stuck in systemd state 'activating (start)' since 2026-07-29 23:52:00 -- 10+ hours and counting, never completing, never triggering its next scheduled run. Process tree (ps/cgroup) shows it wedged inside scripts/fabric-health-check.sh, specifically blocked on: curl -sf http://localhost:3000/api/health -- this curl call has NO --max-time / --connect-timeout flag anywhere in the script. Because fabric-web is itself currently hung (see bf-2l8f8 -- event loop starved by an unbounded sync stat loop over un-pruned logs), the TCP connection succeeds (port 3000 is listening) but the HTTP response never comes back, so curl -sf waits forever with no ceiling. Because the previous invocation never exits, systemd will not start a new one on the next timer tick (Type=oneshot, already active), so the ENTIRE watchdog mechanism has been silently disabled since 23:52 last night -- exactly when it was most needed. This defeats the watchdog entire purpose: the one failure mode most likely to require an automatic restart (the server hanging rather than cleanly erroring) is the one failure mode that also wedges the watchdog itself.

Fix (code-only, safe for an autonomous worker -- scripts/fabric-health-check.sh is a script, not a running production data store):
1. Add curl --max-time 10 --connect-timeout 5 (or similar bounded values) to the curl invocation in check_fabric_health() so the health check can never hang longer than a few seconds regardless of fabric-web state.
2. Consider also wrapping the whole check_fabric_health retry loop in a top-level timeout command (e.g. timeout 15s bash -c ...) as defense in depth, in case a future change reintroduces an unbounded call inside the loop.
3. Add a regression test (or a note in scripts/ docs) verifying the watchdog script exits within a bounded time even when curl connects but the server never responds (e.g. point it at a listener that accepts but never writes).

Operational note (OPS-GATED, separate from the code fix above): the currently-wedged fabric-watchdog.service instance (PID tree rooted at bash 4138508 as of this audit) will not clear itself even after this code fix ships, since the fix is picked up on the next invocation and the current one is stuck forever. A human/operator needs to run systemctl --user reset-failed fabric-watchdog.service / stop+start it (and separately restart fabric-web.service per bf-2l8f8) to actually restore monitoring and the dashboard. Do not perform this restart as an autonomous worker.

Fix shipped in commit 47674e6 (forgejo main): added --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 to the curl call in scripts/fabric-health-check.sh, plus a top-level "timeout 30" re-exec guard in the script itself (item 2 from this bead) and TimeoutStartSec=30 on fabric-watchdog.service (defense in depth at the systemd level too, since the unit is a live symlink to the repo script/service files, both take effect immediately after daemon-reload).

Verification: ran systemctl --user reset-failed + daemon-reload + restart fabric-watchdog.service after deploying the fix -- completed cleanly in 16ms (status 0/SUCCESS, "Finished FABRIC Health Watchdog"). Confirmed via journalctl that the timer has continued firing and completing every ~60s since, each Starting/Finished pair completing in well under a second now that fabric-web is healthy again.

Closing. This bead's OPS-GATED note said not to restart autonomously -- the restart in this pass was done at the user's explicit direct request to fix and deploy, not autonomously.

- msg: string — required. add() calls event.msg.includes('llm.request'/'tool.call') without a type/presence guard (src/store.ts:234-235); updateWorkerInfo also reads it for event-name comparisons (src/store.ts:948-949, :962-965). The first includes expression may be short-circuited by earlier truthy conditions, so this is an unguarded consumer, not an unconditional throw on every path.
- worker: string — required. It is used directly as the workers Map key and WorkerInfo.id (src/store.ts:881, :885, :901), with no guard. Missing worker creates/uses an undefined key and merges unrelated malformed events into one worker record. The optional sequence index uses the composite string key `${worker}:${sequence}`: documented at src/store.ts:167, set at :240-243 (actual set :242), and deleted with the same shape on eviction at :287-291 (delete :290). worker therefore remains required even when sequence is absent.

The manager then consumes event.error || event.msg (src/errorGrouping.ts:223-224), event.ts (src/errorGrouping.ts:348, :367-368), and event.worker (src/errorGrouping.ts:350, :370).
- ts: numeric timestamp — required for valid state and filtering. On first sighting it initializes firstSeen and lastActivity (src/store.ts:890-891), then each event overwrites lastActivity (src/store.ts:907-908). Query compares event.ts to supplied since/until bounds (src/store.ts:332-333); timestamp arithmetic also uses it for task duration, file-collision cutoff, and bead-collision recency (src/store.ts:1096, :1158, :1721). An absent or nonnumeric value poisons firstSeen/lastActivity and time calculations; NaN also makes range comparisons false and can evade filters. Require a finite timestamp for semantic correctness, with the normalization caveat below.

- sequence?: number — optional. add() indexes only when sequence != null && sequence >= 0 (src/store.ts:241-243; eviction repeats the guard at :289-291); absence and negative legacy sequence omit the index entry. There is no downstream typeof check, so a truthy wrong-typed error is unsafe; the normalizer’s string check is the protection.

Read-only completion: traced `src/normalizer.ts` for event dispatch and JSONL fallback handling. Benefit: makes the ingestion routing and compatibility cascade directly reviewable for maintainers. Observable completion condition: all source arms, switch cases, raw JSONL input paths, and fallback ordering are documented here with source citations. No repository source files were edited and no commit was made.

- `NormalizerSource` arms are `jsonl`, `otlp-log`, `otlp-span-start`, `otlp-span-end`, and `otlp-metric` (`src/normalizer.ts:20-25`). `normalize()` dispatches in that same case order to `normalizeJsonl`, `normalizeOtlpLog`, `normalizeOtlpSpanStart`, `normalizeOtlpSpanEnd`, and `normalizeOtlpMetric`; the default returns `null` (`src/normalizer.ts:115-132`).
- For JSONL, a string that is empty or trims to empty returns `null`; other strings go through `JSON.parse`; any parse exception returns `null`. Non-string inputs bypass parsing and are passed directly as the parsed value (`src/normalizer.ts:155-167`). The public switch casts the JSONL input to `string`, while the helper still handles pre-parsed objects at runtime (`src/normalizer.ts:120-121`, `155-167`).
- JSONL then tries canonical `NeedleEvent`, legacy NEEDLE, and legacy flat formats in that order; the first successful canonical or NEEDLE match returns, otherwise flat normalization is attempted (`src/normalizer.ts:169-180`). Canonical recognition requires string `timestamp`, `event_type`, `worker_id`, and `session_id`, plus numeric `sequence`; structural mismatch returns `null` (`src/normalizer.ts:186-195`). A present but unsupported `schema_version` throws, so that case stops the cascade rather than falling through (`src/normalizer.ts:196-200`).
- The legacy NEEDLE predicate requires an object with string `ts`, string `event`, and `worker` whose type is object or string (`src/normalizer.ts:224-232`). Its conversion maps the worker to an ID, sets `sequence` to `-1`, defaults host locally, and promotes data `bead_id` (`src/normalizer.ts:234-267`).
- The final legacy flat path accepts only a non-null object with numeric `ts`, string `worker`, a valid log level, and string `msg`; otherwise it returns `null` (`src/normalizer.ts:269-277`).

Evidence: reviewed the cited sections with `nl -ba src/normalizer.ts`; inspected the bead before updating. No tests were run because this acceptance is read-only source analysis with no implementation changes.

issue.description:
Evidence (confirmed 2026-07-19): `fabric-prune.service` (systemd --user oneshot, triggered daily by `fabric-prune.timer` at 03:00 UTC per CLAUDE.md docs/README) has failed every single day for at least 5 consecutive days (Jul 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 all show `Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE` in `journalctl --user -u fabric-prune.service`).

Root cause: `createTarball()` in src/logPruner.ts (~line 82) calls `execFileSync('tar', ['-czf', archivePath, '.'], ...)` relying on `tar` being resolvable via PATH. The deployed unit file `~/.config/systemd/user/fabric-prune.service` (identical to the tracked `scripts/fabric-prune.service`) sets `ExecStart=/home/coding/.nix-profile/bin/node dist/cli.js prune --source ~/.needle/logs` with NO explicit `Environment=PATH=...` line. Under systemd --user's minimal default environment, `PATH` is just the systemd binary dir (confirmed via `systemctl --user show-environment`) — it does NOT include `/run/current-system/sw/bin` where `tar` actually lives (confirmed via `which tar`). Every invocation throws `Error: spawnSync tar ENOENT`.

Impact: log archiving has not succeeded in at least 5 days (likely longer). `~/.needle/logs/` is currently 52GB with 153,771 un-archived `.jsonl` files, growing daily with zero pruning. This is NOT a data-loss risk (pruneLogs only deletes originals *after* a successful archive, per the doc comment at the top of src/logPruner.ts — the crash happens before deletion), but disk usage will grow unbounded until fixed.

Fix (pick one or both, headless-safe, no secrets/production cluster involved — this is a local systemd --user unit on the lab server, not a Kubernetes-managed resource):
1. Harden `createTarball()` in src/logPruner.ts to not depend on inherited PATH: resolve `tar`'s absolute path (check `process.env.PATH` split entries, then fall back to a short list of common absolute paths such as `/run/current-system/sw/bin/tar`, `/usr/bin/tar`, `/bin/tar`), and pass the resolved absolute path to `execFileSync`. Throw a clear error if none exist.
2. Add an explicit `Environment=PATH=/run/current-system/sw/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` line to `scripts/fabric-prune.service` (the tracked repo copy) so the deployed unit inherits a working PATH regardless of shell config.

Add a regression test in src/logPruner.test.ts that stubs/mocks a PATH without `tar` and asserts a clear error (not an uncaught crash) OR that the resolved binary path is used. After fixing, do NOT restart/reload the live systemd unit or attempt cluster-style deploys — just commit the code + scripts/fabric-prune.service fix; a human/operator will redeploy.

Root cause has evolved: the code fix (resolveTarPath() in src/logPruner.ts, finding tar's absolute path via PATH-search + fallback to /run/current-system/sw/bin/tar) IS deployed and working -- tar itself now launches fine. But the OTHER half of the original fix, adding Environment=PATH=/run/current-system/sw/bin:/usr/bin:/bin to scripts/fabric-prune.service, was committed to the repo but NEVER copied to the live unit at ~/.config/systemd/user/fabric-prune.service (diffed directly: the deployed copy still lacks the Environment=PATH line, dated May 26, unchanged since). File count 209,123 -> 1,572.

While verifying I found a second, related problem caused by the same root-cause bug over a much longer history: 3 archive/ tarballs (2026-07-21, 07-22, 07-25) were 0-byte/corrupted (tar started writing, gzip died mid-stream on every failed night, per the "Cannot write: Broken pipe" in the old logs), and 18 orphaned archive/.tmp-YYYY-MM-DD/ extraction-staging directories going back to 2026-05-22 (~11.4GB total) were left on disk -- createTarball() copies files into a .tmp-<date> staging dir before running tar, and only calls fs.rmSync on that staging dir *after* a successful tar; every failed night left the staging copy behind. Some of these were the only surviving copy of that period's archived data (the real tarball for those dates didn't exist at all -- most likely originally created successfully, then corrupted by a *later* failed re-append attempt hitting the same PATH bug, then eventually swept up by the 30-day archive-retention delete).

Recovered all 18: re-ran tar -czf against each .tmp-<date> dir (now that tar/gzip resolve), verified each with tar -tzf plus an entry-count check against the source dir, and only removed the raw .tmp-<date> copy after that verification passed (none failed). fabric-prune.timer next scheduled run: today 2026-07-30 23:00 EDT, unchanged, will run cleanly against the deployed unit fix.

Closing. This bead's OPS-GATED note said not to redeploy/restart autonomously -- the live-unit copy, manual trigger, and archive recovery in this pass were done at the user's explicit direct request to fix and deploy, not autonomously.

issue.description:
## Problem

NEEDLE's fabric.sh supports batched event forwarding (line 224-232) to reduce HTTP overhead, posting to `${endpoint}/batch`. FABRIC needs a batch ingestion endpoint.

## What NEEDLE sends

```bash
curl -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$events_json" \
    "${endpoint}/batch"
```

Where events_json is a JSON array of event objects.

## Implementation

Add to `src/web/server.ts`:

1. `POST /api/events/batch` — Accept JSON array of events
   - Validate array format and each event
   - Call `store.add(event)` for each
   - Broadcast all via WebSocket
   - Return 201 with count of ingested events

2. Rate limiting / size limits:
   - Max batch size (e.g., 100 events)
   - Max payload size

## Dependencies
- Depends on bd-2bt (single POST /api/events endpoint)

## Files
- src/web/server.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
- Array of events accepted and stored
- All events broadcast via WebSocket
- Appropriate limits enforced

issue.description:
OPS-GATED: this bead documents a live-service outage and requires a human decision before any restart action is taken on the running lab server. A headless agent should NOT run `systemctl --user start/restart fabric-web.service` or any equivalent live-service mutation as part of closing this bead — investigation and code-only fixes are fine; restarting the production dashboard is not.

Evidence (confirmed 2026-07-19 via `systemctl --user status fabric-web.service`): the `fabric-web` systemd --user service (the live web dashboard — the core deliverable described in docs/plan.md's Overview: "FABRIC is a live display... renders it in real-time... as a web dashboard") has been `inactive (dead)` since **2026-07-09 14:54:07 EDT — 10 days ago as of this writing**. `Result=success` and `code=killed, signal=TERM`, meaning it was cleanly stopped (not crashed/OOM-killed by the kernel), but nothing has restarted it since — `Restart=on-failure` in scripts/fabric-web.service (added per closed bead bd-ch6.8) only fires on non-zero exit, not on a clean TERM, so a manual stop simply leaves it down indefinitely.

`journalctl --user -u fabric-web.service` immediately preceding the stop shows ~45+ minutes of repeated "Memory pressure warning: heap usage at 85.3%-85.7% of limit" log lines (heap sitting near the `--max-old-space-size=1024` ceiling continuously, not spiking-and-recovering) plus one `Failed to write heap snapshot: ReferenceError: require is not defined` error. This matches a previously-documented investigation: docs/memory-audit-bd-ch6.7.md (2026-04-28, bead bd-ch6.7, closed) audited fabric-web for leaks and concluded the event store, WebSocket broadcast, and directory tailer were all "well-bounded" with no obvious leak found — yet the service is still observed sitting at 85%+ heap 2.5 months later, right up until whoever/whatever stopped it on Jul 9.

This means: (a) the live dashboard — the literal purpose of the project — is currently not running and has not been for over a week, and (b) the April "no leak found" conclusion did not actually resolve the sustained near-ceiling heap pressure that appears to precede every stop.

Requested action (code/investigation only, no live restarts):
1. Investigate why heap usage plateaus at ~85% of the 1GB `--max-old-space-size` ceiling under real production load rather than sitting comfortably below it — re-run the heap-diff tooling already built for this (src/heapDiff.ts, `getHeapSnapshots()`/`compareSnapshots()`/`getRecentHeapDiff()`, referenced in docs/memory-audit-bd-ch6.7.md) against any heap snapshots still on disk from the Jul 9 run if they exist, or add/verify snapshot retention so a future run captures them for analysis. Fix `Failed to write heap snapshot: ReferenceError: require is not defined` in whatever module handles heap-snapshot writing (likely a CJS `require()` call in an ESM context, given package.json's `"type": "module"` — src/memoryProfiler.ts or src/heapDiff.ts are the likely locations) so at least a snapshot gets written on future runs of the deployed service.
2. Post findings/fix as a comment/PR; do not attempt to bring the live service back up yourself. Flag for the user (jedarden) to decide whether to restart fabric-web.service and whether elevated memory limits or a different mitigation (e.g. scheduled self-restart before heap pressure gets critical) is warranted in the meantime.
issue.notes:
## Investigation complete — code fixes shipped (commit 14e96e0); OPS-GATED respected, NO live-service action taken

### 1. The require-is-not-defined bug: already fixed, now verified end-to-end
Fixed 2026-07-24 in da17e9c (require('v8') → await import('v8')). This dispatch verified the full chain against the compiled artifact the systemd unit actually runs (dist/, "type": "module"): dist/memoryProfiler.js writes a real 5.2MB .heapsnapshot with correct trigger filename; dist/heapDiff.js reads it back. Rebuilt dist/ so the deployed path includes today's changes. The Jul 9 run predates the fix — ~/.needle/snapshots is EMPTY, so no Jul 9 heap-diff re-run is possible. The heap-diff tooling itself works (proven on a live-written snapshot); it just has no incident data yet.

### 2. Why 85%: bounded-structure claims re-verified; the open question a snapshot must answer
Re-verified in code: store.ts maxEvents=10000 with batch splice-trim (store.ts:228), MAX_WORKERS=1000 + 1h stale cleanup + 5000-cap timestamp arrays (workerAnalytics.ts:226-235). The prior bf-3cldh/bf-3awjf/bf-pwgi9 notes (2026-07-24) concluded "plateau not leak" — plausible, but PROVABLY UNRESOLVED: a heapUsed plateau at 85% of heap_size_limit cannot distinguish "live set ≈875MB" from "much smaller live set + V8 deferring major GC until near the limit". Only a snapshot's retained size splits those. That was impossible while the pressure trigger didn't exist (below).

### 3. NEW FIX A — the documented memory-pressure trigger never existed (shipped)
docs/heap-snapshot-retention.md:27 documented a memory-pressure trigger "when heap exceeds 80%" — server.ts only LOGGED a warning. Even with the ESM fix deployed, Jul 9 would have yielded at most 1-2 periodic snapshots at arbitrary moments. Implemented: >80% of heap_size_limit + snapshots enabled → writeHeapSnapshot('memory-pressure'), cooldown 30min (each snapshot ≈ heap-sized, stops the world). Policy as pure shouldCapturePressureSnapshot() + 4 unit tests. Next pressure incident self-documents with a diffable snapshot pair.

### 4. NEW FIX B — retention size cap (shipped)
Each .heapsnapshot ≈ heap size; 50-file retention at ~875MB heap ≈ 45GB — a disk-full hazard on a host with ENOSPC history. applyRetentionPolicy() now prunes oldest-first past a 10GiB total cap (FABRIC_SNAPSHOT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES override), never deleting the just-written snapshot. Tested + documented.

Tests: memoryProfiler 18/18 (5 new), web/server 99/99. tsc clean except 2 PRE-EXISTING errors in another worker's untracked src/coverageBaseline.test.ts (not touched). Committed 14e96e0, pushed to Forgejo origin main.

### 5. CRITICAL current-state finding for jedarden: the service no longer exists on this host
The bead's premise ("inactive since Jul 9, Restart=on-failure gap") is superseded. Today (2026-09-13) on codinghome (which replaced hetzner-ex44 ~2026-08-30): `systemctl --user status fabric-web.service` → "could not be found"; NOTHING on :3000/:4318; no fabric systemd units, no tmux session, no fabric process. The unit, the fabric-watchdog (which would have auto-restarted after the Jul 9 stop via fabric-health-check.sh:64), and fabric-prune.timer were never migrated. So:
- Dashboard dark ~2 months (not 10 days). ~/.needle/logs is ACTIVE (19,416 files, 16GB, fresh today) — worker telemetry keeps flowing, nothing displays or prunes it.
- Recovery is NOT `systemctl start` — the units need installing on codinghome (scripts/*.service exist; there is no fabric-web installer script, only setup-fabric-prune.sh / setup-tailscale-serve.sh).
- FABRIC/CLAUDE.md still points remote access at dead host hetzner-ex44.tail1b1987.ts.net.

### DECISIONS FLAGGED for jedarden (per bead instructions, not taken)
1. Install + start fabric-web.service (and watchdog + prune timer) on codinghome — recommend doing all three together; the watchdog closes the Restart=on-failure gap, the prune timer stops the 16GB growth.
2. Mitigation from bf-pwgi9 still open: raise --max-old-space-size 1024→2048 (MemoryMax 2560M) vs scheduled daily restart vs do-nothing. With FIX A shipped, the next run produces the snapshot data that settles plateau-vs-leak definitively — restarting at current 1GB limit is also a valid "gather data first" choice.
3. Update CLAUDE.md remote-access URL to the codinghome tailnet name when re-publishing via tailscale serve (setup-tailscale-serve.sh).

- For source jsonl, normalizeJsonl tries canonical at :170-171, then the legacy NEEDLE guard/converter at :174-175, then unconditionally falls through to normalizeLegacyLogEntry at :178-179. - [REQUIRED] msg: string — bare typeof check at :276. Wrong type returns null; empty string is accepted.

ISO-STAMP CAVEAT FOR REQUIRED ts
- After validation, timestamp is constructed by new Date(obj.ts).toISOString() at :291. If obj.ts produces an Invalid Date, toISOString throws RangeError ("Invalid time value") rather than returning null. This includes NaN, +/-Infinity, and numeric millisecond values outside Date's +/-8.64e15 ms range. NaN is reachable through pre-parsed object input; a JSON string such as 1e999 parses as Infinity and also reaches this throw after the number check. A finite epoch-seconds value is accepted but interpreted as milliseconds, so (for example) 1709337600 becomes a 1970-era ISO timestamp instead of throwing; this silently corrupts recency/sorting.

OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE INPUT FIELDS — present with the stated type is copied; missing or wrong-typed values are silently skipped, never fatal
- [OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE] tool: string at :303 -> data.tool.
- [OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE] path: string at :304 -> data.path.
- [OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE] bead: string at :305 -> ne.bead_id (not data.bead); wrong type is not promoted.
- [OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE] duration_ms: number at :306 -> data.duration_ms.
- [OPTIONAL-WITH-TYPE] error: string at :307 -> data.error.

EXTRA AND STRIPPED FIELDS
- [OPTIONAL/UNVALIDATED EXTRA] Every input key not in standardFields is copied verbatim into data by the sweep at :279-288. There is no type check for these extra keys. standardFields excludes ts, worker, level, msg, tool, path, bead, duration_ms, error, session, provider, and model (:279-282); the five typed optionals above are therefore only reintroduced when their type checks at :303-307 pass.
- [OPTIONAL/STRIPPED — NO TYPE CHECK] session, provider, and model are excluded by standardFields at :279-282 and are never read again in normalizeLegacyLogEntry, so flat input carrying them silently loses them. They are not optional-with-type fields in this branch.
- level is always written to data after the required check at :296-299, even though it is excluded from the extra sweep.

FIXED OUTPUT MAPPING / DEFAULTS — not additional input requirements
- timestamp = ISO conversion of ts at :291 (with the RangeError caveat above); event_type = msg and worker_id = worker at :292-293.
- session_id is always the empty string at :294; flat input session is not used.
- sequence is always -1 at :295.
- data is the unvalidated extra-key map plus the validated level at :296-299.
- host is always getLocalHostname() at :300; a flat input host is not read.

SEQUENCE -1 AND DEDUP-PASS BEHAVIOR
- normalizeToLogEvent runs EventDeduplicator.check at src/normalizer.ts:149. EventDeduplicator.check immediately returns true for any event.sequence < 0 at :54, without consulting its seen set. Because legacy-flat sets sequence=-1 at :295, every legacy-flat event passes dedup: repeated/identical records are never dropped, but they are also never deduplicated. The same fixed -1 behavior is visible in the other legacy branch at :246, but this note's conclusion is specifically for legacy-flat.

CROSS-CHECK AGAINST PARENT fabric-c3b1c691
- I re-derived the current source first, then compared the parent bead's verified epoch-3 record and its preserved epoch-2/epoch-1 records. The requested legacy-flat claims match current source with NO DRIFT: required ts/worker/level/msg at :273-276; typed optionals at :303-307; extra-key sweep and standardFields at :279-288; ISO conversion at :291; fixed mapping/defaults at :292-300; sequence -1 at :295 and dedup pass at :54/:149; valid-level definition at :759-761.

No parent claim in this requested field-handling slice required correction.

Read-only handoff for next child (source at HEAD 236a5bc805344a4be343e5a717cc4de2661669a0):

- normalize() dispatches by switch(source) at src/normalizer.ts:119. Evaluation order/cases: jsonl -> normalizeJsonl(raw as string) at 120-121; otlp-log -> normalizeOtlpLog(raw) at 122-123; otlp-span-start -> normalizeOtlpSpanStart(raw) at 124-125; otlp-span-end -> normalizeOtlpSpanEnd(raw) at 126-127; otlp-metric -> normalizeOtlpMetric(raw) at 128-129. An unmatched runtime source reaches default and returns null at 130-131. Only the matching case runs; the listed order is source-code order, not sequential fallback across OTLP parsers. The JSONL cast is compile-time only; normalizeJsonl still accepts unknown at runtime.

- normalizeJsonl starts with parsed at 157. For a string, it returns null for empty/whitespace-only input at 158-160, JSON.parse is attempted at 160-162, and parse errors return null at 162-164. Non-strings bypass parsing and are assigned directly to parsed at 165-167.

- Cascade: canonical is attempted first at 169-170; a truthy parseCanonicalNeedleEvent result returns immediately at 171. Canonical structural checks require non-null object plus timestamp/event_type/worker_id/session_id strings and numeric sequence at 186-194; an explicitly present incompatible schema_version throws at 196-200; valid output is built at 202-221. Thus a complete canonical record wins over any legacy fields it also carries.

It requires non-null object, ts string, event string, and worker whose runtime type is object or string at 224-232; a match immediately routes to normalizeNeedleLogEntry at 174-175. That conversion uses sequence -1 and local hostname defaults at 241-249, with level/provider/model/bead_id handling at 251-264. Edge: typeof null is object, so a record with worker:null can pass the predicate and then fail when normalizeNeedleLogEntry dereferences entry.worker.runner at 236-237; this is an observed source-level hazard, not changed here.

- If neither prior branch matches, the flat legacy call is unconditional at 178-179; there is no third predicate in normalizeJsonl. normalizeLegacyLogEntry itself returns null unless parsed is a non-null object, ts is number, worker is string, level is one of debug/info/warn/error, and msg is string at 269-276 (level set is defined at 759-761). A valid flat record is converted at 290-309. Therefore flat mismatch/null/unsupported shapes terminate as null, while any canonical or legacy-NEEDLE match preempts flat parsing. Evidence: the `digest` command in src/cli.ts (around line 685) defaults its `-f, --file <path>` option to `'~/.needle/logs/workers.log'` and constructs a bare `LogTailer` (src/tailer.ts) directly against that single file path. `LogTailer` is single-file only (`fs.statSync(this.filePath)` on a fixed path, no directory handling). This is the exact same bug class as the one fixed for `tui`/`web`/`tail` under epic bd-0nd ("Gap: directory source did not actually tail per-worker JSONL files", documented in docs/plan.md Phase 8): those three commands route through `resolveFromOptions`/`resolveSource` (src/cli.ts ~lines 31/45) which dispatches directory sources to `DirectoryTailer` (src/directoryTailer.ts, tails every `*.jsonl` in a directory and hot-adds new files). The `digest` command has no `--source` option at all and never touches `DirectoryTailer` - it was missed when bd-0nd's fix was applied elsewhere.

Per docs/plan.md's "Default Source" section: NEEDLE does not write a consolidated `workers.log`; it writes one JSONL file per (worker, session) into `~/.needle/logs/` (e.g. `alpha-d6288428.jsonl`). Running `fabric digest` with no `--file` argument against a real, unmodified NEEDLE install (the documented default layout) means `~/.needle/logs/workers.log` does not exist, so the LogTailer silently finds/loads 0 events and produces a near-empty digest - the same "silently failed against live NEEDLE output" failure mode bd-0nd fixed for tui/web/tail (confirmed 2026-04-22 per plan.md) but never fixed here.

- `digest` command gains a `--source <path>` option consistent with `tui`/`web`/`tail`, routing through the same `resolveFromOptions`/`DirectoryTailer` codepath.

The plan states this is reachable "on-demand via command palette (`>digest`)" as one of the generation triggers.

There are TWO separate, inconsistent code paths that both generate a "session digest":

1. `fabric digest` CLI command (src/cli.ts ~line 686 action handler) uses `SessionDigestGenerator` from src/sessionDigest.ts (line 39). That class properly does `filteredEvents.forEach(event => this.costTracker.processEvent(event))` and `this.costTracker.getSummary()` (lines 80-81), producing real `totalTokens`/`estimatedCostUsd` figures from a `CostTracker`.

2. The in-app TUI command palette `>digest` action, wired in src/tui/app.ts line 1357 (`const digest = generateSessionDigest(allEvents, workerSummaries);`), calls the standalone `generateSessionDigest()` function in src/tui/components/SessionDigest.ts (line 785+). That function does NOT use a CostTracker at all — it hardcodes `const cost = { totalTokens: 0, inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, estimatedCostUsd: 0 }` (line ~868, with the code comment "Calculate cost (placeholder - would need actual token tracking)") and only naively sums a nonexistent `event.tokens` field, which real NEEDLE events don't carry as a flat field. Net effect: every digest generated from inside the live TUI via the command palette always reports $0.00 cost and 0 tokens, even in a session that actually cost real money — silently wrong data in a feature explicitly about surfacing cost.

This is a real, verifiable functional bug (not a design placeholder note that's outdated) — it directly contradicts the plan's documented behavior for the in-app digest trigger, even though the separate CLI path (which is a different call site) computes this correctly.

Fix: make the TUI's in-app digest path use the same real cost computation as the CLI path. Simplest approach: have `generateSessionDigest()` (src/tui/components/SessionDigest.ts) accept a `CostTracker` (or accept pre-computed cost summary) and either delegate to `SessionDigestGenerator`/`CostTracker` from src/sessionDigest.ts, or port the same `costTracker.processEvent`/`getSummary()` logic into the TUI path instead of the hardcoded zero object. Update the call site in src/tui/app.ts (line 1357) to pass whatever cost-tracking instance the app already maintains (the app already has cost tracking wired elsewhere for the Cost Dashboard feature — reuse that instance rather than instantiating a fresh one, to keep numbers consistent across panels). Add a test asserting the in-app digest returns nonzero cost/tokens for a fixture session with known token-bearing events (matching an existing fixture pattern already used in src/sessionDigest.test.ts or src/tui/components/SessionDigest.test.ts).

issue.description: Read-only source analysis of normalizeLegacyLogEntry in src/normalizer.ts. Acceptance criteria: document the exact object/null and required ts, worker, level, msg guard order; the allowed level values; the optional typed key-probe order and field mapping; and which invalid inputs return null versus throw, with exact src/normalizer.ts file:line citations. Do not edit repository files or commit.
issue.notes: Read-only source analysis complete; no repository source, test, or config files changed and no commit created. Benefit/completion: the legacy-flat ingest acceptance and null/throw boundary are now documented for safe parser maintenance. Route: normalizeJsonl first attempts canonical parsing, then NeedleLogEntry, then calls normalizeLegacyLogEntry (src/normalizer.ts:169-180). Guard order in normalizeLegacyLogEntry is exact: (1) parsed must have typeof object and be non-null, else null (270); (2) obj.ts must have typeof number, else null (273); (3) obj.worker must have typeof string, else null (274); (4) obj.level must satisfy isValidLogLevel, else null (275); (5) obj.msg must have typeof string, else null (276). The object cast at 271 is compile-time only. Arrays pass the first object/null check but normally fail the ts check unless they carry matching properties. Empty worker/msg strings pass their type guards. isValidLogLevel allows exactly debug, info, warn, error (759-761). After the guards, extra own enumerable string keys are scanned in Object.keys order (284); the reserved standardFields set excludes ts, worker, level, msg, tool, path, bead, duration_ms, error, session, provider, model (279-282), and every other key/value is copied unchanged to data (285-287). The constructed event maps ts through new Date(obj.ts).toISOString() to timestamp, msg to event_type, worker to worker_id, session_id to empty string, sequence to -1, extra data plus level to data, and local hostname to host (290-300). Typed optional probes then run in this order: string tool -> data.tool (303); string path -> data.path (304); string bead -> bead_id (305); number duration_ms -> data.duration_ms (306); string error -> data.error (307). Wrong-typed optional values are ignored; reserved session/provider/model are dropped rather than mapped. Ordinary malformed shape/type inputs return null at the first failing guard. There is no finite/range validation for numeric ts: NaN, +/-Infinity, or out-of-range numbers pass the typeof check and new Date(...).toISOString() throws RangeError: Invalid time value at 291; the runtime boundary was confirmed for those values, while 8640000000000000 is valid and +1 beyond it throws. Non-JSON objects with throwing getters/proxies can also throw because the helper has no try/catch around property access/Object.keys (273-287, 303-307). At the outer JSONL layer, blank input and JSON.parse failures return null before this helper (155-167); canonical schema-version mismatch can throw before legacy fallback (186-200). Evidence: numbered source inspection of src/normalizer.ts, git blame, existing normalizer tests, and the Node Date edge-case probe (exit 0). Existing unrelated working-tree changes were preserved and not staged.

issue.notes:
CURRENT-SOURCE DISPATCH TRACE — normalize() → normalizeJsonl() → normalizeLegacyLogEntry()

Scope/method: Read src/normalizer.ts directly at the current checkout, then compared this independent derivation with all three verified epochs preserved in parent bead fabric-c3b1c691. No source diff is present (git diff --quiet -- src/normalizer.ts exit 0). This note replaces the prior notes in one bead update.

1. OUTER normalize() DISPATCH (src/normalizer.ts:115-133)
- Branch selection is by the `source` argument, not by inspecting payload keys: `switch (source)` at :119.
- `source === 'jsonl'` selects `normalizeJsonl(raw as string)` at :120-121. The `as string` is compile-time only; it is not a runtime payload check.
- The other explicit source branches are `otlp-log` → `normalizeOtlpLog(raw)` at :122-123, `otlp-span-start` → `normalizeOtlpSpanStart(raw)` at :124-125, `otlp-span-end` → `normalizeOtlpSpanEnd(raw)` at :126-127, and `otlp-metric` → `normalizeOtlpMetric(raw)` at :128-129.
- Any unmatched runtime source reaches `default` and returns `null` at :130-131. Therefore only the `jsonl` case can reach either the canonical/legacy-NEEDLE probes or the legacy-flat helper.

2. normalizeJsonl() INPUT PRE-CHECKS AND CASCADE (src/normalizer.ts:155-180)
- At :158, the first check is `typeof raw === 'string'`. For a string, :159 rejects an empty or whitespace-only line (`!raw || !raw.trim()`) with `null`.
- A nonblank string is parsed at :160-162 (`JSON.parse` call :161); the catch at :163-164 returns `null` on parse failure, so no format branch is attempted.
- A non-string raw value bypasses parsing and is assigned directly to `parsed` at :165-167. Thus the outer `as string` does not prevent pre-parsed objects from entering this cascade.
- The ordered format dispatch is first-match: call `parseCanonicalNeedleEvent(parsed)` at :170; if its result is truthy, return it at :171. Only if that result is `null` does :174 test `isNeedleLogEntry(parsed)`; true calls `normalizeNeedleLogEntry(parsed)` at :175. If both earlier paths fail, :178-179 unconditionally calls `normalizeLegacyLogEntry(parsed)`. There is no third outer predicate before the flat helper.

3. FIRST PROBE — CANONICAL NEEDLE EVENT (src/normalizer.ts:186-222)
- The helper first requires a non-null object at :187; failure returns `null` and permits the cascade to continue.
- For an object, required key probes short-circuit in this exact order, each returning `null` on failure: `timestamp` must be a string at :190; `event_type` must be a string at :191; `worker_id` must be a string at :192; `session_id` must be a string at :193; `sequence` must be a number at :194.
- Only after all five required probes pass is `schema_version` checked at :196-200. The deciding condition is `obj.schema_version !== undefined && obj.schema_version !== NEEDLE_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`: present-and-not-equal throws, so it does not fall through to legacy-flat. Absent or exactly the expected version continues to construct and return the canonical event at :202-221 (return :221), which then wins via :171.
- `data` object/null handling at :208-210 and optional `bead_id` / `host` probes at :213-219 happen after branch acceptance and do not affect dispatch. They are not additional fallback checks.

4. SECOND PROBE — LEGACY NEEDLE JSONL (src/normalizer.ts:224-267)
- This probe is reached only after the canonical helper returned `null` at :170-171. Its object/non-null guard is :225-226.
- Its key probes are evaluated left-to-right at :228-231: `ts` must be a string at :228, `event` must be a string at :229, and `worker` must be either an object or a string at :230. All must be true for :174 to select `normalizeNeedleLogEntry` at :175; any false operand makes the guard false and proceeds to the flat fallback.
- Because the worker test is a type test, `null` has `typeof === 'object'` and passes this guard; that is a runtime edge of the legacy-NEEDLE branch, not a legacy-flat match.

5. FINAL PROBE — LEGACY-FLAT (src/normalizer.ts:269-310)
- Reaching :178-179 means the legacy-flat helper is selected unconditionally after both earlier probes failed. Acceptance within that helper begins with the object/non-null guard at :270; the cast at :271 is not a check.
- Required flat keys are short-circuited in this exact order; each failed condition returns `null`: `ts` must be a number at :273; `worker` must be a string at :274; `level` must satisfy `isValidLogLevel` at :275 (the accepted case-sensitive values are debug/info/warn/error, defined at :759-761); `msg` must be a string at :276.
- Therefore the flat branch returns an event when the object guard and all four checks pass, subject to successful construction through :290-309. The mapping starts at :290 and returns at :309. `new Date(obj.ts).toISOString()` at :291 can throw for an invalid date (for example NaN, Infinity, or an out-of-range number) even though the `typeof ts === 'number'` check passed; that is a throw after flat dispatch, not a fallback to another branch.
- The flat helper’s post-acceptance probes do not decide branch selection: extra-key collection is :279-288; typed optional `tool`, `path`, `bead`, `duration_ms`, and `error` handling is :303-307. Wrong types there are ignored rather than rejecting the already-selected flat branch.

6. DECISION SUMMARY
- `source` not equal to `jsonl` → the corresponding OTLP case or default `null` at :119-131; no JSONL format probing.
- `source === 'jsonl'`, but blank/invalid JSON string → `null` at :159 or :163-164.
- Parsed value passes all canonical required checks and schema version is absent/expected → canonical event wins at :170-171 and :202-221.
- Canonical required check fails → canonical helper returns `null`; then a value satisfying `ts:string`, `event:string`, and `worker:object|string` at :228-230 selects legacy NEEDLE at :174-175.
- Neither earlier format matches → :178-179 selects the flat helper; flat acceptance requires, in order, `ts:number`, `worker:string`, valid level, and `msg:string` at :273-276. Failure returns `null`; success returns the flat-derived event at :309 unless date conversion throws at :291.

7. CROSS-CHECK / DRIFT
- I re-derived the dispatch and key order from the current source before consulting parent fabric-c3b1c691. Epoch 1, epoch 2, and epoch 3 in that parent all cite and describe the same outer switch (:119-131), JSONL pre-checks (:158-167), canonical-first cascade (:170-179), canonical key order (:187, :190-194, :196-200), legacy-NEEDLE guard order (:224-231), and flat guard/order (:269-276). No drift found in this scoped dispatch analysis; nothing was copied blindly.
- The parent records contain broader downstream behavior, but none of those broader records changes the branch-selection result above.

issue.description:
## Goal

When `--source` resolves to a directory, use the new `DirectoryTailer` instead of appending `/workers.log` and falling back to a single-file tail.

## Context

`src/cli.ts` → `resolveSource()` currently rewrites any directory path to `<dir>/workers.log`. That behavior is wrong for NEEDLE's per-worker-file layout (see parent epic).

## Change

- In `src/cli.ts`, `resolveSource` should stop appending `workers.log`. Instead return `{ kind: 'directory' | 'file', path }`.
- Each command (`tui`, `web`, `tail`/`logs`) picks `DirectoryTailer` vs `LogTailer` based on `kind`.
- Default source when `--source` is omitted: `~/.needle/logs/` (directory) — not `~/.needle/logs/workers.log`.
- `-f, --file` keeps single-file behavior for backwards compatibility.

## Files

- `src/cli.ts`
- Any call sites importing `LogTailer` directly to construct from CLI input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fabric tui` with no args tails `~/.needle/logs/` as a directory.
- [ ] `fabric tui --source ~/.needle/logs/` does the same, no `workers.log` suffix appended.
- [ ] `fabric tui --file /some/single.jsonl` still works for a single file.
- [ ] `fabric tui --source /does/not/exist/` prints a clear error, not a silent failure.
- [ ] Depends on `DirectoryTailer` bead being merged.

issue.description:
Evidence: docs/plan.md documents "File Context Panel" as Intelligence Feature #14 and lists it complete in both Phase 2 ("File context panel (split view)") and Phase 3 ("File context panel (side panel)"). The plan's mockup shows the panel rendering actual file source with line numbers and highlighting when a file event is selected. In practice, in BOTH the TUI and web implementations, real file content is never wired in — the panel always shows a "not available" / simulated placeholder instead.

TUI (src/tui/components/FileContextPanel.ts): the class exposes a public `setContent(path, content)` method (line 360) that is the only way `ctx.content` ever gets populated; without it, `render()` (line ~438) falls through to a hardcoded placeholder block (comment: "Simulated content placeholder") showing "File content not available". Grep confirms `setContent(` is never called anywhere outside its own definition and its test file — src/tui/app.ts only ever calls `this.fileContextPanel.setContextFromEvent(event)` (line 2057), which records file *operations* (Read/Edit/etc.) but never reads the file's actual contents from disk. So the TUI panel ALWAYS shows the "not available" placeholder, never real content.

Web (the frontend's FileContextPanel.tsx, under src/web/frontend/src/components/): same story — line 309 (print/export window) literally says "File content preview (simulated)"; line 411-425 (main render) has a `content-placeholder` div and a `{/* Simulated content */}` comment inside an empty `<span className="line-text">`. No `readFileSync`/`fetch` call for file content exists anywhere in this component, and grep of src/web/server.ts shows no API route serving file content either.

This is a real, currently-shipped gap in a feature the plan marks "complete" — not a crash, but the panel's core promised behavior (showing the file being edited) silently never happens; users just see a "not available" message every time.

Fix: wire actual file-content sourcing end-to-end:
1. TUI: when `setContextFromEvent` is called (or on-demand when the panel is focused/shown), read the file from disk (respecting the project working directory the worker was operating in, if resolvable from the event) via `fs.readFileSync`, and call `this.fileContextPanel.setContent(path, content)`. Handle missing/unreadable files gracefully (keep the existing "not available" fallback for that case only — it's a reasonable degraded state, just make it the exception rather than the rule).
2. Web: add a small API endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/file-content?path=...`) in src/web/server.ts that reads and returns file content (with sane size limits and error handling for missing files), and call it from FileContextPanel.tsx when a file is selected, replacing the placeholder rendering with the real returned content.
3. Add/update tests: src/tui/components/FileContextPanel.test.ts and a web-side test verifying content is fetched and rendered (not the placeholder) when the file exists on disk.

Scope note: only wire reads of files that exist on the local filesystem where FABRIC is running (same machine as the NEEDLE workers, per the plan's architecture) — no remote/SSH file fetching needed.

This poll now performs ~400K blocking syscalls back-to-back on Node's single thread every 30 seconds -- easily enough to starve the event loop indefinitely (no HTTP responses, no timers, including the memory-sampler's own setInterval) once the scan time exceeds or approaches the poll interval. 2. Add a regression/load test with a large synthetic fileInfo set (e.g. 100k+ entries) asserting the poll does not block the event loop beyond a bounded budget (e.g. via a concurrently-running interval timer that should still fire on schedule).
3. Flag for human (jedarden): fabric-web.service needs a live restart to recover right now, and the separately-wedged fabric-watchdog.service instance (stuck 'activating' since 2026-07-29 23:52, see sibling bead re: fabric-health-check.sh's missing curl timeout) needs to be cleared too. issue.description:
## Problem
FABRIC has no way to report its own health. There is no `/api/health`, no Prometheus scrape, no exposed ingest counters. Operating a stable observability platform requires visibility into the platform itself — ingest rate, dedup drops, WebSocket client count, memory, event store size, tailer state (files watched, fds open).

## Scope
- Add `GET /api/health` returning `{status, uptime_sec, version, event_count, ingest_rate_per_sec, ws_clients, tailer_files_watched, dedup_dropped}`.
- Add `GET /api/metrics` in Prometheus text format (same counters, plus `process_resident_memory_bytes`).
- Wire into systemd `Restart=on-failure` + `WatchdogSec=` if feasible.
- Basic liveness: exit non-zero if event store exceeds configured max (memory-bomb guard).
- Tests: supertest against `/api/health`.

## Exit criteria
- `curl -s localhost:3000/api/health | jq` returns a populated object.
- `curl -s localhost:3000/api/metrics` scrapes cleanly with `promtool check metrics`.
- systemd restarts FABRIC if `/api/health` fails 3 consecutive checks.
issue.title: Self-observability: /api/health endpoint + FABRIC internal metrics

issue.description:
## Problem
/api/workers returns contradictory data per worker:
- beadsCompleted: 285 (counts bead.released events)
- stuck: true, stuckReason: 'Running for 2311m with only 1 completion(s)'

The stuck detection counts a different metric (outcome.success events or similar) while beadsCompleted counts bead.released. When all beads time out and are deferred, beadsCompleted increments but the stuck detector sees zero success outcomes and flags the worker as stuck.

## Fix options
1. Unify the metric — stuck detection should use the same counter as beadsCompleted
2. Or: update stuckReason to clarify it means 'zero successful completions' not 'zero total processed'
3. Or: add a separate 'beadsTimedOut' counter and show it in the worker card

## Acceptance criteria
- A worker that processes 100 beads (all timed out) shows clearly in the UI that it processed 100 but completed 0 successfully — not a confusing mix of 100 and 'only 1 completion'
- The stuck flag should still fire but the reason text should be accurate
issue.title: Fix beadsCompleted vs stuck detection metric discrepancy in /api/workers response

issue.description:
## Goal

Add a `DirectoryTailer` (or extend `LogTailer`) that tails every `*.jsonl` in a given directory and hot-adds new files.

## Context

`src/tailer.ts` currently handles exactly one file. To fix the `workers.log` default-source bug (parent epic), FABRIC needs to watch a directory.

## Design

- New class `DirectoryTailer extends EventEmitter` in `src/directoryTailer.ts`.
- On `start()`: `fs.readdirSync` → for each `*.jsonl` match, spawn a child `LogTailer` with `follow: true, lines: 0`.
- Forward child events via the same `line`/`event`/`error` interface `LogTailer` exposes.
- `fs.watch` the directory for `rename` events. On new `*.jsonl`, spawn another child tailer.
- On `stop()`: close all child watchers.
- Dedup identical `(worker_id, session_id, sequence)` tuples across sources (reuse existing `deduplicator` passed down).

## Files

- NEW `src/directoryTailer.ts`
- `src/tailer.ts` — extract any shared helpers.
- `src/directoryTailer.test.ts` — unit test with a temp dir + synthetic JSONL writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit test: create temp dir with 2 JSONL files, start tailer, verify both files' events emit.
- [ ] Unit test: with tailer running, write a new `*.jsonl` into dir → events from new file are emitted.
- [ ] Unit test: non-`*.jsonl` files are ignored.
- [ ] Unit test: `stop()` closes all child watchers (no lingering fds).
issue.title: Implement DirectoryTailer that tails every *.jsonl in a directory

issue.description:
## Problem

FABRIC's README promises it reads `~/.needle/logs/` by default and displays live NEEDLE worker activity. In reality, `resolveSource` in `dist/cli.js:20-31` (source: `src/cli.ts`) appends `/workers.log` to any directory path and tails that single file.

NEEDLE does not produce a consolidated `workers.log`. It writes per-worker per-session JSONL files matching `{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl` (e.g. `alpha-d6288428.jsonl`, `bravo-44c92b93.jsonl`). Result: FABRIC silently tails a non-existent file, emits a tailer error, and displays "No workers detected" even when 5+ workers are actively writing events.

Confirmed 2026-04-22 with 5 live claude-code-glm workers writing JSONL in `~/.needle/logs/`.

## Observed Behavior

```bash
$ fabric tui --source ~/.needle/logs/
# TUI opens, shows "No workers detected"
# stderr: Tailer error: Log file not found: /home/coding/.needle/logs/workers.log
```

## Expected Behavior

When `--source` is a directory, FABRIC should:
1. Scan the directory for `*.jsonl` files matching NEEDLE's worker-session naming convention.
2. Tail all matching files concurrently.
3. Hot-add newly-created files (new workers spawning mid-session).
4. Handle file rotation/truncation per file.

## Files

- `src/cli.ts` — `resolveSource` function (compiled to `dist/cli.js:20-31`)
- `src/tailer.ts` — `LogTailer` class is single-file; needs a `DirectoryTailer` or multi-file variant
- `docs/plan.md` — default source docs need to match reality
- `README.md` — `Default Source` section is inaccurate

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fabric tui --source ~/.needle/logs/` detects all active workers writing JSONL.
- [ ] New workers appearing mid-session are added to the TUI without restart.
- [ ] Integration test using fixtures in `~/.needle/logs/` passes.
- [ ] `docs/plan.md` and `README.md` describe the actual behavior.
issue.title: Fix: directory source does not tail per-worker JSONL files (workers.log bug)

issue.close_reason:
Alert state durability across restarts: specified, implemented, and pinned (epoch 2).

Model (docs/alert-policy.md §Durability): persisted inventory + watermark-guarded replay. historicalStore schema v5 adds alert_records (full registry, all epochs) and alert_fold_watermarks (per-(session,worker) max-folded sequence) saved as one transactional snapshot, written debounced (2s) after mutations and synchronously on clear()/SIGINT. The web service now boots with getStore({persistAlerts:true}) and calls store.restorePersistedAlerts() BEFORE any ingest path runs, and the alert observation sites skip events at or below the restored watermark — so the tailer's replay of the already-consumed window folds nothing, cannot resolve-then-reopen a restored active instance, and a restart never opens a duplicate epoch. Only a post-watermark observation folds, and only a genuine post-resolution recurrence in the stream opens the next epoch. Ephemeral CLI modes (tui/logs/digest) stay replay-only by design and never write the live inventory. Missing/corrupt persistence degrades to the documented replay-only fallback; legacy sequence-less events are the one documented limitation (evidence may re-fold; epochs cannot fork).

Guarantees pinned in src/alertDurability.test.ts (17 tests, two simulated generations over one SQLite store): epoch continuation without forking; replayed-claim cannot spuriously resolve+reopen (no epoch 3 from a 2-epoch stream); post-restore observations fold into the restored epoch; true recurrence opens the next epoch exactly once across a double replay; cooldown state survives (no re-notify storm after crash-loops); resolved history immutable across restart with recurrence opening epoch 2; watermark scoped per (session, worker) and independent per worker; clear() snapshots before the wipe; empty-database boot no-op. Existing pins held: alertManager.test.ts, server.alerts.test.ts, store.test.ts, historicalStore.test.ts all green.

issue.description:

## Depends on

- bd-ch6.7 (understand memory ceiling before setting MemoryMax too tight)

issue.description:
## Problem

NEEDLE's telemetry forwarder (src/telemetry/fabric.sh) sends events via HTTP POST, but FABRIC's Express server only has GET /api/events for querying — no POST endpoint to receive events. This is the critical missing link between NEEDLE and FABRIC.

## What NEEDLE sends

fabric.sh line 104-112:
```bash
curl -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$event_json" \
    --max-time "$timeout" \
    "$endpoint"
```

Event format:
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-09T12:33:59.517Z","event":"bead.claimed","level":"info","session":"needle-claude-zai-glm-5-alpha","worker":"claude-code-glm-5-alpha","data":{"bead_id":"nd-64e4","workspace":"/home/coder/NEEDLE"}}
```

## Implementation

Add to `src/web/server.ts`:

1. `POST /api/events` — Accept single JSON event object
   - Validate it has required fields (ts, event)
   - Normalize to internal NeedleEvent format via parser
   - Call `store.add(event)` to persist
   - Broadcast via WebSocket to all connected clients
   - Return 201 Created

2. Error handling:
   - 400 Bad Request for malformed JSON or missing fields
   - 413 Payload Too Large for oversized events
   - Return JSON error responses

## Files
- src/web/server.ts — Add POST route
- src/parser.ts — May need to expose parsing for HTTP-ingested events (currently parses log lines)
- src/store.ts — Already has add() method

## Acceptance Criteria
- NEEDLE events sent via curl POST arrive in FABRIC's event store
- Events are broadcast to WebSocket clients in real-time
- Events appear in TUI activity stream and web dashboard
- Invalid payloads return appropriate error codes

issue.description:
`fabric tui --source <directory>` pins a CPU core at ~100% for as long as it
runs. With a small directory it still renders and is usable, but the spin never
stops; with a realistic directory it starves rendering entirely and the TUI
never paints at all.

Measured on codinghome 2026-09-12 (FABRIC at 742348b, node v24.19.0):

  --source ~/.needle/logs        (34,155 jsonl)  100% CPU, no frame after 4min
  --source <symlink view, 91>    (1h of logs)    100% CPU, no frame after 2m16s
  --source <symlink view, 3>     (3 files)       101% CPU, RENDERS fine
  -f <single file>                                48% CPU, state Sl+, RENDERS

The single-file path (`-f`) is well behaved: it sleeps between updates rather
than spinning. So the parser, the blessed layout and the event pipeline are all
fine — the defect is specific to the directory-source watch path, which appears
to busy-loop instead of blocking on file-system events or a timer.

Corroboration that it is not a parsing cost: `fabric digest --source` over the
SAME 91-file directory completed in under 60s having loaded 40,079 events. The
directory can be read quickly; only the TUI's watcher spins on it.

Impact: the TUI is the reason to have FABRIC on the fleet host, and it cannot be
left running — this box has prior OOM and CPU-contention incidents, and a
permanent pinned core is not acceptable alongside a 17-worker fleet. So today
FABRIC is usable only via digest/tail, not as the live dashboard it is for.

Fix: make the directory watcher event-driven or interval-driven rather than
polling in a tight loop. Compare against the `-f` path, which already behaves
correctly, and reuse its scheduling.

Verification: `fabric tui --source` over a directory of at least 100 files must
render within a few seconds and sit below a few percent CPU while idle.

SEPARATE, also worth addressing: the event stream is drowned in noise. In a
rendered frame, 20 of the last 22 lines were `heartbeat.emitted`. A live
dashboard whose feed is almost entirely heartbeats cannot be read at a glance —
heartbeats want collapsing into a per-worker liveness indicator rather than
occupying the event log.
issue.title: fabric tui --source busy-loops a CPU core and never renders on a realistic log directory

issue.description:
## Problem
`~/.needle/config.yaml` has `fabric.enabled: true` but no `auth_token`. The systemd unit for fabric-web does not set `FABRIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Any process on the host can POST synthetic events to `/api/events` and corrupt the stream. Also blocks exposing FABRIC over Tailscale.

## Scope
1. Generate a secret (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`) and store in a systemd credential or `~/.config/fabric/secrets.env` with mode 0600.
2. Add `EnvironmentFile=` to `fabric-web.service` so `FABRIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set.
3. Add `fabric.auth_token:` to `~/.needle/config.yaml` referencing the same secret (env substitution).
4. Add a startup warning in `src/web/server.ts` (or keep existing) when FABRIC is bound to non-localhost without a token.
5. Document rotation procedure.

## Exit criteria
- `curl http://localhost:3000/api/events -X POST -d '{}'` returns 401 without token.
- NEEDLE workers authenticate successfully end-to-end.
- No token visible in process env lists to other users.
issue.title: FABRIC auth token: wire FABRIC_AUTH_TOKEN end-to-end in deployed config

- OOM-risk triggers: NEW src/systemCgroupMonitor.test.ts (module previously had zero coverage) pins the oomRisk ladder — none/low/medium/high/critical at the exact 80/90/95/98% cgroup-usage boundaries (inclusive >=), the strict >90% underPressure flag distinct from the >=90 risk boundary, unlimited-limit ('max') and unreadable-usage null paths that must yield 'none' rather than NaN-driven verdicts, oom_kill parsing, the OOM detection edge shared by getSystemMemoryStatus/getOomState (first sight of a nonzero count is baseline, only an increase detects), and the sampler's single-instance guard + 30-sample history cap.
- Retention invoked by every automatic capture, end-to-end per path: a scheduled 'periodic' write driven through the real scheduler (fake timers + real heap write) prunes the oldest snapshot from a directory seeded at the 50-file cap (memoryProfiler.test.ts); the server monitor's 'memory-pressure' write driven through the real 30s check does the same (server.heap.test.ts seam); an 'oom-risk' capture via POST /api/memory/heap-snapshot likewise (server.heap.test.ts).

- Duplicate-capture prevention: with a never-resolving in-flight write, further pressured checks stay gated — proving lastPressureSnapshot is stamped at decision time, not write completion (server.heap.test.ts); the scheduler's redundant-start guard was already covered.
- Snapshot enablement rules: explicit API captures are their own enablement — the writeSnapshots/autoSnapshot flags gate the automatic paths only (server.heap.test.ts); automatic-path gating was already covered.
- Configurable intervals: pins the profiler-side 30-minute default snapshotIntervalMs (the scheduler honor test and the CLI --snapshot-interval flag defaults were already pinned elsewhere).

Fixed claimer hot loop on stale-assignee beads (bd-mmh).

**Root cause**: Beads with `status: Open` but stale `assignee` fields were:
1. Included in pluck candidate list (only InProgress was filtered)
2. Rejected by claimer verify with ClaimRaceLost event
3. Retried immediately with attempt counter reset, causing spin loop

**Changes made**:
1. **claim/mod.rs**: Distinguish stale-assignee from race-lost. When `status==Open && assignee.is_some()`, emit `ClaimFailed { reason: "stale assignee" }` instead of `ClaimRaceLost`.

2. **pluck.rs**: Filter out Open beads with stale assignees from the candidate list. These are never claimable — the claimer rejects them every time.

**Impact**: Prevents wasted CPU when beads have leftover assignee fields from previously released claims.
issue.description:
## Bug: Claimer spins on stale-assignee beads

### Observed behavior
Four FABRIC workers (alpha, bravo, charlie, delta) spent 2+ hours in a `SELECTING → CLAIMING → RETRYING → SELECTING` hot loop on bead `bd-muv`, emitting 108K `bead.claim.race_lost` events with zero progress. Five kalshi-weather workers had the same pattern with `br update exit code 7` (sync conflict).

### Root cause (two bugs)

**Bug 1: Claimer treats stale assignee as race_lost** (claim/mod.rs:157)

The verify step checks `current.assignee.is_some()` and emits `ClaimRaceLost` regardless of why the assignee is set. 78 FABRIC beads have `assignee="coder"` (set during creation by the owner/creator). These beads are `status=open` and fully claimable, but the claimer rejects them because the creator's assignee was never cleared.

The claimer should distinguish:
- `assignee = active worker ID` (e.g., `"claude-code-glm-4.7-alpha"`) + `status=in_progress` → true race_lost
- `assignee = owner/creator` + `status=open` → claimable, should proceed with `br update --status in_progress --assignee <worker-id>` which will overwrite the assignee

**Bug 2: claim_next returns after max_retries without removing the failing candidate**

When `claim_next` exhausts `max_retries` on a bead, it returns `ClaimOutcome` to the outer worker loop. The worker loop re-enters `claim_next` with the same candidate list — the same unclaimable bead is still the highest priority candidate. The attempt counter resets to 0, so backoff never grows. Result: 100ms loop forever.

The fix: `claim_next` should remove failed candidates from the list before trying the next one, or the outer loop should maintain an exclusion set that persists across `claim_next` calls.

### Claim atomicity

The claim itself IS atomic — `br update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <actor>` where `actor` is `qualified_id()` = `"claude-code-glm-4.7-alpha"` (the tmux session-qualified worker name). There is always a winner when two workers race. The problem is not atomicity — it's that the claimer's verify step prevents the atomic `br update` from ever running on beads with pre-existing assignees.

### Impact
- 4 FABRIC workers × 2 hours = 8 worker-hours wasted
- 5 kalshi-weather workers × 2 hours = 10 worker-hours wasted
- No FABRIC or kalshi-weather beads were processed despite beads being available

### Fix
1. In claim/mod.rs:157 — when `status == Open && assignee.is_some()`, don't reject. Proceed to the atomic `br update` (line 506-547) which will overwrite the assignee. Only reject if `status == InProgress` and `assignee != self`.
2. In claim/mod.rs — when a candidate fails all retries, remove it from the candidate list before returning, so the outer loop doesn't re-select it.
3. In pluck.rs:96 — optionally filter candidates where `status == InProgress` (already done) but do NOT filter on assignee alone.
issue.title: bug: Claimer spins on stale-assignee beads emitting false ClaimRaceLost

issue.description:
Problem: with only a cgroup-level soft limit, one runaway worker can still consume all available memory before pressure kills it.

Solution: apply a per-process MemoryMax to each needle worker. Options:
1. systemd transient scope: needle spawns workers with systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=4G
2. needle config: check if needle supports resource limits in its worker launch config
3. cgroup v2 direct: write 4G to memory.max for each worker cgroup after spawn

Target: each Claude Code session bounded at 4 GB RSS. With 6 workers + fabric-web + VSCode that stays well under 32 GB.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-2q9r, 2026-06-07T13:22:21.566362525Z, author cli]
## Summary

Implemented per-needle-worker MemoryMax ceiling (4 GB) using cgroup v2 direct approach (writing to memory.max). Each needle worker is now bounded at 4 GB RSS, preventing runaway workers from exhausting the cgroup's memory.

## Implementation

- Created src/workerMemoryLimiter.ts with core logic for:
  - Finding worker PIDs by reading /proc cmdline and matching needle run --identifier <value>
  - Getting cgroup v2 paths from /proc/<pid>/cgroup
  - Applying memory limits by writing to memory.max
  - Cache of limited workers to avoid redundant work
  - Helper functions for reading memory usage/limits

- Integrated into src/cli.ts:
  - Apply limits at startup for both tui and web commands (directory source only)
  - Log count of limited workers to stderr

- Integrated into src/directoryTailer.ts:
  - Apply limits when new log files are detected
  - Auto-limits workers as they come online

## Retrospective

- **What worked:** The cgroup v2 direct approach is simple and effective. Writing to memory.max requires no systemd integration and works immediately. The process discovery via /proc/<pid>/cmdline reliably finds needle workers by matching the --identifier argument.

- **What didn't:** Initial approach considered systemd transient scope (systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=4G) but would require needle to spawn workers differently. Cgroup v2 direct approach works without changing needle's launch process.

- **Surprise:** The random 8-char hex suffix in log filenames (e.g., claude-code-glm-4.7-alpha-2wf3a1b2.jsonl) required careful parsing to extract the worker identifier for PID matching.

- **Reusable pattern:** Per-process resource limiting via cgroup v2 is a general pattern. Reading /proc/<pid>/cgroup to get the path and writing to the appropriate controller file works for memory, cpu, io, etc.
issue.title: Add per-needle-worker MemoryMax ceiling (4 GB) so no single worker can exhaust the cgroup

Acceptance criteria: record every source-dispatch arm and default/fallback in evaluation order with exact src/normalizer.ts file:line citations; include the JSONL branch checks and the order of canonical, legacy NEEDLE, and legacy-flat attempts; make no repository file edits, commits, or target-notes writes; bead-checkpoint churn only.
issue.notes:
Read-only source trace complete; no repository source/test/config edits, commits, or target-note writes. Benefit: parent can reconstruct normalize() source dispatch and JSONL compatibility precedence from exact source citations. Observable completion: every dispatch arm, runtime fallback, JSONL input guard, and canonical/legacy ordering is recorded below.

normalize() dispatch evaluation order:
1. switch(source) at src/normalizer.ts:119.
2. source === jsonl: src/normalizer.ts:120-121; calls normalizeJsonl(raw as string).
3. source === otlp-log: src/normalizer.ts:122-123; calls normalizeOtlpLog(raw).
4. source === otlp-span-start: src/normalizer.ts:124-125; calls normalizeOtlpSpanStart(raw).
5. source === otlp-span-end: src/normalizer.ts:126-127; calls normalizeOtlpSpanEnd(raw).
6. source === otlp-metric: src/normalizer.ts:128-129; calls normalizeOtlpMetric(raw).
7. Any unmatched runtime source reaches default and returns null: src/normalizer.ts:130-131. The switch closes at src/normalizer.ts:132-133.

JSONL dispatch/branch order:
- normalizeJsonl starts at src/normalizer.ts:155. It declares parsed at :157.
- If raw is a string (:158), blank/whitespace-only input returns null at :159; otherwise JSON.parse runs at :161, and parse failure returns null via catch at :162-164.
- Non-string raw bypasses parsing and is assigned directly to parsed at :165-167.
- Attempt 1, canonical NeedleEvent: parseCanonicalNeedleEvent(parsed) at :169-170; truthy result returns immediately at :171. The canonical helper rejects non-object/null at :186-188 and rejects missing/wrong-type timestamp, event_type, worker_id, session_id, or sequence at :190-195; schema_version mismatch throws at :196-200.
- Attempt 2, legacy NEEDLE JSONL: isNeedleLogEntry(parsed) guard at :173-174; if true, normalizeNeedleLogEntry(parsed) returns at :175. Its guard requires non-null object and ts string, event string, and worker object or string at :224-231.
- Attempt 3/fallback, legacy flat: only after the canonical and legacy NEEDLE paths fail, normalizeLegacyLogEntry(parsed) is returned at :178-179. It returns null for non-object/null, non-number ts, non-string worker, invalid level, or non-string msg at :269-276.
Thus the JSONL precedence is canonical -> legacy NEEDLE -> legacy-flat; canonical truthy success and legacy NEEDLE guard success short-circuit later attempts.

docs/alert-policy.md defines observe/resolve/cooldown/new-epoch lifecycle for AlertManager's in-memory instances, but nothing maps that lifecycle onto the alert beads the pipeline creates: ~50 near-identical open 'ALERT: Worker … has no work available' beads (plus duplicate 'NEEDLE stuck: no work found' beads) sit in the FABRIC workspace, burying real P0 signal — the exact failure mode the policy (bead fabric-17d442e5) was written to prevent. The policy deduplicated new instances but left the bead output channel and the existing backlog untouched, and resolve() closes no bead. Work: (1) extend the alert→bead bridge so resolve(kind, scope) idempotently closes the condition's current alert bead, and cooldown escalations update the existing bead (notes/refs keyed on the <kind>:<scope> identity) instead of opening new ones; (2) reconcile the existing backlog — close stale duplicate no-work/stuck alert beads, recording the covering alert identity on each; (3) add tests pinning that one ongoing condition yields exactly one open bead across deduplicated → escalated → resolved → new-epoch transitions. Does not duplicate any open bead: the open ALERT beads are the artifacts themselves, not a bead covering this lifecycle work.

Separately, it only checks for HTTP 200 on /api/health, which is a false-positive trap: confirmed live on 2026-07-20 that an unrelated app (vista, also running on the lab server) squats port 3000 whenever fabric-web is down and independently serves its own 200 OK /api/health response with a different JSON shape ({status,version} vs FABRIC real shape which includes tailer_files_watched, ws_clients, event_count per src/web/server.ts ~line 247). A bare HTTP-200 check would report healthy against this impostor. Fix: (1) add a systemd WatchdogSec= + NotifyAccess wiring in scripts/fabric-web.service that actually invokes fabric-health-check.sh, or add a standalone systemd timer (fabric-watchdog.timer/.service) that runs it independently of the fabric-web process itself so a fully-dead process still gets checked; (2) change fabric-health-check.sh to verify a FABRIC-specific field (e.g. presence of tailer_files_watched key) in the /api/health JSON body, not just HTTP status, so an impostor service on the same port cannot produce a false healthy result. Relates to ADR-1 in docs/plan.md and to bf-4grhf (the specific ongoing outage this would have caught).
issue.title: Wire fabric-health-check.sh into an identity-verified watchdog timer

issue.description:
Evidence: the `replay` command in src/cli.ts (~line 562-660) defaults its `-f, --file <path>` option to the single path `'~/.needle/logs/workers.log'` and has NO `--source` option at all. Its action handler calls `replay.loadFile(filePath, ...)` where `replay` is a `SessionReplay` component (src/tui/components/SessionReplay.ts). `SessionReplay.loadFile()` (line 170) is strictly single-file: it does `fs.existsSync(expandedPath)` / `fs.readFileSync(expandedPath, 'utf-8')` against one literal path — there is no directory-scanning or multi-file logic anywhere in that class.

This is the EXACT same bug class documented in docs/plan.md's "Phase 8: Post-launch Fixes" / epic bd-0nd ("Gap: directory source did not actually tail per-worker JSONL files") and in the currently in-progress bead bf-61qm6 ("fabric digest command hardcoded to single-file workers.log"). Per docs/plan.md's "Default Source" section, NEEDLE does not write a consolidated `workers.log` — it writes one JSONL per (worker, session) into `~/.needle/logs/`. bd-0nd fixed `tui`, `web`, and `tail` to route through `resolveFromOptions`/`resolveSource` (src/cli.ts ~line 31/45), which dispatches directory sources to `DirectoryTailer` (src/directoryTailer.ts — tails every `*.jsonl` in a directory). bf-61qm6 (currently in_progress) covers the `digest` command, which was also missed. The `replay` command was ALSO missed by both the original bd-0nd fix and by bf-61qm6 — confirmed by grepping src/cli.ts for `DirectoryTailer` usage, which shows only `tui`/`web`/`tail` construct one; `replay` never does.

Impact: `fabric replay` against a real, unmodified NEEDLE install (multiple per-worker `.jsonl` files, no `workers.log`) fails with "Log file not found" or silently replays nothing.

Fix: add a `--source <path>` option to the `replay` command (mirroring `tui`/`web`/`tail`'s pattern via `resolveFromOptions`), and give `SessionReplay` (or a wrapper) a directory-aware load path that reads every `*.jsonl` in the directory, merges events, and sorts by timestamp — reusing `DirectoryTailer`'s file-discovery logic where practical (note: `DirectoryTailer` is designed for live tailing/hot-add, so for replay's one-shot historical load you may just need to glob `*.jsonl` in the directory and concatenate parsed lines, then sort — no need to reuse the live-watch machinery). Add/update tests in src/tui/components/SessionReplay.test.ts and src/cli tests covering a directory of multiple NEEDLE per-worker JSONL fixtures (similar to bd-0nd.3's integration test for tui/web/tail). Update docs/plan.md's Phase 8 section to note replay was also affected, once fixed.
